problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(2)=-1,\,{f}^{′}(2)=-2,\,g(2)=-5,\,{g}^{′}(2)=1
$$

If $h(x)=\frac{5f(x)+4}{g(x)+6},$ find the value of ${h}^{′}(2).$

feedback.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(1)=8,\,{f}^{′}(1)=6,\,g(1)=4,\,{g}^{′}(1)=4
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=1} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(1)g(1)-f(1){g}^{′}(1)}{{g}^{2}(1)} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 4-8\cdot 4}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
